contangent.definition: Traumatic injuries that involve rips or tears in your body's tissues. While skin lacerations are the most common, these wounds can happen to tissues inside your body, too. They can even happen without the laceration affecting the outside of your body.

A common, often chronic, musculoskeletal symptom characterized by discomfort ranging from dull aches to sharp, shooting sensations in the spine, nerves, or muscles, frequently causing limited mobility.
Feeling of discomfort anywhere in your belly region — the area between your ribs and pelvis.
Pain or discomfort in the area between the neck and belly. Chest pain may be sharp or dull. It might come and go, or you might always feel the pain. The exact symptoms depend on the cause.

A chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistently high levels of sugar (glucose) in the blood. It occurs when the body cannot produce enough insulin or cannot use the insulin it produces effectively.

An abnormal connection between an artery and a vein. Normally, blood flows from arteries to capillaries, and then to veins. In an AV fistula, this capillary network is bypassed, allowing high-pressure blood to flow directly from the artery into the vein.

An abnormal tangle of blood vessels that causes problems with the connections between your arteries and veins. AVMs most often occur in the spinal cord and in the brain but can develop elsewhere in the body.
A highly contagious disease marked by the acute onset of fever (102–104 °F), severe aches and pains, prostration, inflammation of the mucous membranes of the respiratory tract, and severe headache.

A highly contagious liver infection caused by the Hepatitis A Virus (HAV). It leads to liver inflammation and is typically spread through the ingestion of contaminated food or water, or through close personal contact with an infected individual.

A genetic bleeding disorder caused by a deficiency or absence of blood clotting Factor VIII. This missing protein prevents blood from clotting effectively, leading to prolonged or excessive bleeding from minor injuries, surgery, or spontaneous internal bleeding into joints and muscles.

Direct connections between arteries and veins. In the integument, they are well documented in the glabrous skin of the hands and feet where they are involved in temperature control in the thermoneutral range between 26°C and 36°C.
A pain in your head or face that's often described as a pressure that's throbbing, constant, sharp or dull. Headaches can differ greatly in regard to pain type, severity, location and frequency.

The swelling of the lymphatic tissues located at the back of the throat and nasal passage. While normal-sized tissues help filter germs, enlargement (hypertrophy) often occurs due to chronic infections, allergies, or physiological growth in young children

A minor variant of normal adult hemoglobin, typically making up about 2% to 3.5% of total hemoglobin in healthy adults. It is composed of two alpha and two delta globin chains and is usually measured via High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) or capillary electrophoresis.

contangent.disease: Atrial tachycardia - paroxysmal with av block
contangent.definition: A specific type of rapid, irregular heart rhythm. It occurs when the heart's upper chambers (atria) beat extremely fast (150 to 200 beats per minute), but the atrioventricular (AV) node blocks some of these electrical signals from reaching the lower chambers (ventricles).
Feeling of discomfort discomfort in the area between the lower ribs and the buttocks, typically caused by muscle strains, ligament injuries, or wear and tear in the spine.

A mood disorder that causes a persistent feeling of sadness and loss of interest. Also called major depressive disorder or clinical depression, it affects how you feel, think and behave and can lead to a variety of emotional and physical problems.
A rare, idiopathic or drug-induced autoimmune blistering disease characterized by the linear deposition of IgA at the dermoepidermal junction.
Any discomfort felt in or around the knee joint—where the thigh bone meets the shin bone. It can range from mild, temporary muscle strains to chronic conditions like arthritis.

Viruses and bacteria that infect your respiratory tract above your vocal cords. Symptoms can include a runny or stuffy nose, sore throat or headache. Common colds, strep throat and sinus infections are all examples of upper respiratory infections.
Pain or inflammation in or around a tooth, its supporting gums, or the jaw. It ranges from mild, temporary sensitivity to severe, throbbing pain that impacts sleep and daily activities.
A common classification indicating that your red blood cells have Type A antigens and the Rhesus (Rh) factor.
An enlarged area in the lower part of the body's main artery, called the aorta. The aorta goes from the heart through the center of the chest and belly area, called the abdomen.

A condition in which your airways narrow and swell and may produce extra mucus. This can make breathing difficult and trigger coughing, a whistling sound (wheezing) when you breathe out and shortness of breath.

Shortness of breath or difficult, uncomfortable breathing. It is a subjective feeling that you cannot get enough air into your lungs, often described as air hunger, chest tightness, or a sensation of working harder to breathe.

A temporary inflammation of the trachea and major bronchi (the airways of the lungs). It causes swelling, excess mucus production, and a persistent cough that usually lasts for one to three weeks. It is primarily a viral infection

A sore throat (pharyngitis) is a scratchy or burning feeling in the back of your throat. It may hurt to swallow or talk. Most sore throats happen because of a viral infection, like the common cold or flu. In addition to the soreness, you may have symptoms like a cough or runny nose. Most sore throat symptoms go away within three to 10 days.

A short-term inflammation or infection of the cavities around the nasal passages (sinuses). It causes the sinuses to become swollen and clogged with mucus, leading to facial pain, pressure, and congestion.

A spreading skin infection, most commonly of the lower leg. It's caused by bacteria entering through a break in the skin. The affected skin is swollen, painful and warm to the touch. The infection can cause a fever and become very serious, involving deeper tissues.

An inflammation and infection of the air-filled space behind the eardrum (the middle ear). It typically occurs when viruses or bacteria multiply in mucus or fluid trapped in the ear due to blocked Eustachian tubes.

A buildup of a pus that can affect any part of your body. There are many different types of abscesses. They can occur on your skin, in your mouth or around your organs. Skin abscesses may look red and swollen. Bacterial infections usually cause abscesses.
Usually caused by an injury, repetitive overhead movements, or poor posture. Common culprits include rotator cuff strains (inflamed tendons), bursitis (inflamed fluid sacs), or frozen shoulder.

A chronic digestive condition that occurs when stomach acid or contents flow backward into the esophagus. This repeated backwash irritates and can damage the lining of the food pipe. It is a persistent, more severe form of occasional acid reflux.
A collision or incident involving one or more motor vehicles that results in damage, injury, or loss.
Discomfort in any of the structures in the neck. These include the muscles, nerves, bones (vertebrae), joints, and the discs between the bones.
A natural emotion characterized by feelings of tension, worried thoughts, and physical changes like increased blood pressure.
An area of the skin that has changes in texture or color and may look inflamed or irritated. The skin may be red, warm, scaly, bumpy, dry, itchy, swollen, or painful. It may also crack or blister.
A chronic metabolic condition where the body cannot use insulin properly (insulin resistance) and eventually cannot produce enough insulin.

Any feeling of discomfort, aching, or pain anywhere in the lower limbs, typically between the groin and the ankle. It can be acute (sudden and temporary) or chronic (long-lasting), and range from a mild ache to severe, debilitating pain that impacts mobility.
An imbalance in the vaginal microbiome. It occurs when naturally occurring 'good' bacteria (lactobacilli) decrease, allowing harmful 'bad' anaerobic bacteria to overgrow.

An allergic reaction that causes sneezing, congestion, itchy nose and watery eyes. Pollen, pet dander, mold and insects can lead to hay fever symptoms. Hay fever can make you feel awful, but you can find relief with lifestyle changes, allergy medications and immunotherapy (allergy shots).
A pattern of drinking that causes harm or distress to your life.
A common heart condition where major blood vessels supplying the heart become damaged, narrowed, or blocked by plaque buildup (cholesterol and fatty deposits).
A progressive, long-term lung condition that causes inflammation and damage to the airways and air sacs, making it progressively harder to breathe.
A broad term used to describe sensations of feeling woozy, lightheaded, or unsteady.

An inflammation of the tissues in your sinuses (spaces in your forehead, cheeks and nose usually filled with air). It causes facial pain, a stuffy or runny nose, and sometimes a fever and other symptoms.

Any illness you get from a virus (a small germ that uses your cells to reproduce). Common viral illnesses include colds, the flu, COVID-19, norovirus (“stomach flu”), HPV (warts) and herpes simplex virus (cold sores).

The inflammation of the lining of the stomach and small or large intestines. Often called the 'stomach flu', it is commonly triggered by a viral, bacterial, or parasitic infection, and results in abdominal cramps, watery diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting.
The forceful retrograde expulsion of gastric contents from the body.
Any discomfort, stiffness, or soreness in the ankle joint, heel, arches, or toes.

Any discomfort, tenderness, or stiffness in or around the hip joint—where the thigh bone (femur) meets the pelvis. It can be dull or sharp and is often felt in the groin, thigh, buttocks, or knee rather than directly on the joint itself.
A serious chronic medical condition where the heart doesn't pump blood as efficiently as it should, leading to fluid buildup (congestion) in the lungs and body.

Abnormally high levels of lipids (fats), such as cholesterol and triglycerides, circulating in your blood. Excess fats can build up in artery walls as plaque (atherosclerosis), drastically increasing your risk of heart attacks and strokes.
A feeling of pain or discomfort in the chest, typically the front of the chest. It may be described as sharp, dull, pressure, heaviness or squeezing.
A headache that can cause intense throbbing pain or a pulsing feeling, usually on one side of the head. It often happens with nausea, vomiting, and extreme sensitivity to light and sound.
An inflammatory condition of the vulva and vagina caused by the overgrowth of Candida yeast, most commonly Candida albicans.

An overwhelming state of constant exhaustion or lack of energy that does not go away with rest or sleep. It is different from normal tiredness, severely limiting your ability to function, think clearly, or engage in daily activities.
An injury that occurs when the strong ligaments supporting the joint stretch beyond their limits or tear. It usually happens when you roll, twist, or turn your ankle awkwardly.
Also known as Hyperglycemia (high blood sugar) is common in people who have diabetes.
A general term for discomfort or aching located in the lowest part of the abdomen and pelvis, between the hips and below the navel.
A sudden, temporary loss of consciousness and muscle control. It typically happens when a brief drop in blood pressure reduces blood flow to the brain, followed by a fast and complete recovery.
An acute worsening of respiratory symptoms—such as increased dyspnea (shortness of breath), cough, and sputum production—that goes beyond normal day-to-day variations.
Bleeding from the uterus occurring outside pregnancy in reproductive-aged women that is abnormal in the parameters of regularity, frequency, volume, or duration.
feeling of discomfort in the heel, arch, toes, or sole, usually caused by overuse, injury, or underlying conditions like arthritis.

Once known as juvenile diabetes or insulin-dependent diabetes, is a chronic condition. In this condition, the pancreas makes little or no insulin. Insulin is a hormone the body uses to allow sugar (glucose) to enter cells to produce energy.
Any sensation of discomfort, pressure, or aching in one or both ears. The pain can feel dull, sharp, or burning, and ranges from mild irritation to severe.

Abnormal buildup of excess fluid trapped in the body's tissues. Gravity naturally causes this fluid to pool in the lower extremities, specifically the feet, ankles, and legs, causing the area to appear puffy or swollen.
A sudden, short-term infection of the middle ear. It occurs when viruses or bacteria become trapped in fluid behind the eardrum, causing inflammation and pain.
A general term for conditions that cause inflammation of the skin.

A pocket of pus that's caused by a bacterial infection. The abscess can occur at different areas near the tooth for different reasons. A periapical (per-e-AP-ih-kul) abscess occurs at the tip of the root. A periodontal (per-e-o-DON-tul) abscess occurs in the gums at the side of a tooth root.
Irregular uterine tightenings that occur during pregnancy—particularly in the third trimester—without causing cervical dilation or leading to actual childbirth.
Any discomfort, aching, or stiffness experienced anywhere from your shoulder down to your wrist and fingers.

An itchy, inflammatory skin condition triggered by direct physical contact with an irritating substance or an allergen. It causes a distinct rash confined to the specific area that touched the trigger.
A clear or whitish fluid that comes out of your vagina. Discharge is normal, but changes in the amount, consistency, color or smell could be a sign of an infection or other problem.

An injury where muscle fibers stretch beyond their limits or tear. It occurs due to overuse, over-stretching, or sudden powerful contractions, and typically results in localized pain, swelling, and reduced mobility.
A sudden or gradual deviation from a person's normal baseline level of awareness, cognition, or consciousness.
Pain, scratchiness, or irritation of the throat that often worsens when you swallow.
A sensation of discomfort, cramping, or aching in the side and back of your body, located specifically between the bottom of your ribs and the top of your hips.
A skin condition that occurs when your hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells. It causes whiteheads, blackheads or pimples.

Any damage to the muscles, bones, tendons, or ligaments located between the knee and the ankle. These injuries typically result from sudden trauma (accidents or sports impacts) or gradual overuse, leading to pain, swelling, and reduced mobility.
Any discomfort, aching, or soreness in the fingers, palm, or back of the hand.
Any trauma that damages the scalp, skull, brain, or underlying tissue and blood vessels in the head.

A false sensation of motion, where you feel like you or your surroundings are spinning or moving when there is no actual movement. It is a symptom of an underlying balance disorder, often originating from issues with the inner ear or the brain, rather than a disease itself.
Feeling of discomfort or burning located in the upper central abdomen, just below the ribs and above the navel.
Swelling and irritation, called inflammation, of the tonsils. The tonsils are two oval-shaped pads of tissue at the back of the throat.
A person has tested positive for the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), indicating the virus is present in their body.
Often caused by sprains or fractures from sudden injuries.
Inflammation or infection of the vagina and sometimes the vulva. It typically causes symptoms like itching, burning, pain, and abnormal discharge.
Ophthalmalgia is another name for eye pain.
Feeling of discomfort, pain, or aching in any joint in the body.
A chronic, complex medical disease characterized by an abnormal or excessive accumulation of body fat that poses a risk to health.

A common skin condition that happens when hair follicles become inflamed. It's often caused by an infection with bacteria. At first it may look like small pimples around the tiny pockets from where each hair grows (hair follicles).

An ongoing, also called chronic, condition. It's caused by the human immunodeficiency virus, also called HIV. HIV damages the immune system so that the body is less able to fight infection and disease.
Any traumatic damage or chronic strain affecting the structures of the hand, including the skin, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, nerves, and blood vessels.
The natural, unintentional loss of a pregnancy before the 20th week of gestation.
The unpleasant, subjective sensation of discomfort in the stomach and the urge to vomit.
Any damage to the bones, muscles, tendons, or ligaments within the shoulder joint and the upper arm.
A chronic condition that causes skin discoloration and itchy rashes. It usually starts in childhood, and flare-ups can continue through adulthood.
An inflammation of the cervix, the lower, narrow end of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

The cells collected from your cervix look unusual under a microscope. It does not mean you have cancer. Most abnormal results are caused by minor cell changes from the Human Papillomavirus (HPV), inflammation, or common infections, and frequently resolve on their own.

Raised, itchy welts on the skin. They can appear as small bumps or large patches and range in color from red to flesh-toned. They are typically triggered by an allergic reaction or the release of histamine in the body.
A medical emergency that occurs when blood flow to an area of the brain is interrupted or reduced. This deprives brain tissue of oxygen and nutrients, causing brain cells to die within minutes.
A skin condition that causes dry and itchy patches of skin. It’s a common condition that isn’t contagious. Symptoms of eczema can flare up if you contact an irritant or an allergen.
A reduction of the total body mass, by a mean loss of fluid, body fat (adipose tissue), or lean mass (namely bone mineral deposits, muscle, tendon, and other connective tissue).
A sudden, often severe inflammation of the pancreas
A chronic disorder characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain, profound fatigue, and sleep, memory, and mood issues.
An inflammation of the transparent membrane that lines the eyelid and eyeball.
Injury or damage to nerve roots in the area where they leave the spine.
An infection of the reproductive organs of people assigned female at birth. It most often happens when sexually transmitted germs spread from the vagina to the uterus, fallopian tubes or ovaries.
An individual who regularly inhales and exhales the smoke produced by burning tobacco or other plant materials rolled in a paper wrapper.
A common condition where abdominal tissue, such as fat or part of the intestine, protrudes through a weak spot in the lower abdominal muscles, often resulting in a noticeable bulge in the groin.
s a painful, pus-filled bump that forms under the skin when bacteria infect a hair follicle

Tenderness, throbbing, sharp, stabbing, burning pain or tightness in the breast tissue. The pain may be constant or it may occur only occasionally, and it can occur in men, women and transgender people.
A common blood disorder that occurs when the body lacks sufficient iron to produce adequate hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that transports oxygen throughout the body.
A break or crack in one or more of the bones that make up the ankle joint.
The levels of specific enzymes, proteins, or substances measured in your blood fall outside the standard reference range.
An injury to either a muscle or tendon, while a back sprain is the stretching or tearing of a ligament.

contangent.disease: Fluid in the ear (otitis media - serous)
Lou Gehrig's disease (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis; ALS)
Infection of the vulva and vagina
Clot on heart or vessel wall (mural thrombus)
